events.name: CusCampbell
events.info: CusCampbell is an R&B artist, singer-songwriter, and trombonist combining smooth vocals, modern R&B production, and live instrumentation. He first gained national attention after Snoop Dogg co-signed him during Peace Out 2020, a Facebook Watch special hosted by Keke Palmer and David Dobrik. He later appeared alongside Grammy Award-winning artist Jon Batiste in a viral TikTok campaign. Since then, he has performed for the WNBA and Boston Mayor Michelle Wu, collaborated with Sha Money XL, and continues to headline tours across North America.

events.name: Lyal Strickland
events.info: Lyal Strickland Monday, November 9th Lyal Strickland is an Americana singer-songwriter whose music is as authentic as the Ozark hills from which it hails. With a background deeply embedded in the rural landscapes of Missouri, his lyrics resonate with the experiences of small-town life, weaving tales of struggle, resilience, and the unyielding human spirit. Strickland's songs are a testament to his commitment to his roots and his versatility as an artist. His albums move through stages of life, showcasing his distinctive voice that brings his narratives to life. Each song is a window into Strickland's world, inviting listeners to step into stories woven with candor and humility.

SplinterMount , ME::YOU
events.info: SplinterMount and ME::YOU Tickets $15 or PWYC SplinterMount is olula negre (cello/voice), Torstein Johansen (bass), Alex Henry (sax), and Grace Harper (piano). The group explodes the atomic centers of tone, timbre, and texture, reassembling the shards into a cohesive, emotive whole. SplinterMount was born from the musical incubator that is the monthly Outlab improv sessions at Clevelands Bop Stop.The quartet pieces together the multiple influences brought by each member, layering them to craft a sound that uses the language of free improvisation, while constantly pushing against the boundaries of that language. SplinterMount has opened for such artists as Tatsuya Nakatani and Jessica Pavone. ME::YOU is the collaborative project of Cleveland artists LaToya Kent and RA Washington, whose work examines the social and historical possibilities of experimental popular music through an intentionally intimate framework. Emerging from years of collaboration within Mourning [A] BLKstar, the duo foregrounds improvisation, minimal production, and the expressive potential of the voice, drawing from post-punk, industrial music, dub, hip-hop, free improvisation, noise, and Black vernacular musical traditions without treating these genres as fixed categories.Their compositions function as sites where personal narrative, embodied performance, and sonic experimentation converge, revealing how Black experimental practice continually reshapes the boundaries between popular music, avant-garde expression, and everyday life.
